Definition: of Latin origin (libra); a pound in weight:--pound.
BiblicalUsage: lítra means a pound in weight, and its few appearances are all worth reading. In John 19:39, "about an hundred pound [weight]."; and in John 12:3, "Then took Mary a pound of ointment of spikenard".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a pound of spikenard is the measure of love — Mary poured it on Jesus' feet, and Nicodemus brought a hundred pound to His burial.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
